scenes.visual: Title card 'The Loop Inside the Line' over a pale cross-section of a forested valley. COLOUR MAP, same in both films and the lesson: dashed GOLD line = the boundary; BLUE arrows = inputs crossing in; RED arrows = outputs crossing out; GREY ring of arrows = the internal loop inside the line; TEAL 'N' blocks = nitrogen; GOLD 'P' blocks = phosphorus. Cream background, 16:9. Numbers appear only as on-screen text. Valleys, trees, microbes and lakes are simple labelled cartoons marked 'schematic'; the counter values are computed from the lesson's numbers.

scenes.tts: Where does the nitrogen in a cut forest's stream come from? Cut a forest, keep it from growing back, and its stream carries far more nitrogen than before.
scenes.visual: Cartoon valley: left half forested, right half cut stumps with logs lying on the ground. A stream runs out of the cut side; TEAL 'N' blocks in the water multiply as it flows. A large '?' over the stream.
scenes.narration: Where does the nitrogen in a cut forest's stream come from? Cut a forest, keep it from growing back, and its stream carries far more nitrogen than before.

scenes.tts: Nobody added fertiliser, and the logs stayed where they fell. To find the source, keep accounts, the way a bank does. First, draw a line around the valley.
scenes.visual: Reset to the whole forested valley. A dashed GOLD line draws itself around it, from the canopy top down to the bedrock. Label 'boundary'. A small bank-style counter appears top right reading '0 kg N per hectare'.
scenes.narration: Nobody added fertiliser, and the logs stayed where they fell. To find the source, keep accounts, the way a bank does. First, draw a line around the valley.

scenes.tts: Inside the line, nitrogen sits in pools, such as the soil and the trees. A pool is like a bank balance. A flux is a transfer, like a deposit or a withdrawal.
scenes.visual: Inside the line, three labelled boxes pulse: 'soil organic N', 'soil ammonium and nitrate', 'trees'. Caption tags: 'pool = amount (kg per hectare)'; an arrow between two boxes flashes with 'flux = kg per hectare per year'.
scenes.narration: Inside the line, nitrogen sits in pools, such as the soil and the trees. A pool is like a bank balance. A flux is a transfer, like a deposit or a withdrawal.

scenes.tts: Here nitrogen crosses the line in two ways. From the air, rain and snow deposit eight kilograms per hectare each year. Microbes fix six more.
scenes.caption: Here nitrogen crosses the line in two ways. From the air, rain and snow deposit 8 kg per hectare each year. Microbes fix 6 more.
scenes.visual: Two BLUE arrows cross the GOLD line from above: '8 deposition' and '6 fixation' (illustrative numbers). TEAL N blocks ride along them into the valley.
scenes.narration: Here nitrogen crosses the line in two ways. From the air, rain and snow deposit 8 kg per hectare each year. Microbes fix 6 more.

scenes.tts: It leaves in two ways. The stream carries three away, and microbes release two to the air as gas.
scenes.caption: It leaves in two ways. The stream carries 3 away, and microbes release 2 to the air as gas.
scenes.visual: Two RED arrows cross the GOLD line outward: '3 stream' at the valley mouth, '2 gas (denitrification)' rising from wet soil.
scenes.narration: It leaves in two ways. The stream carries 3 away, and microbes release 2 to the air as gas.

scenes.tts: The store changes only by what crosses the line. Change in stock equals inputs minus outputs. This forest gains nine kilograms of nitrogen per hectare each year. The line and the year must be stated before any adding.
scenes.caption: The store changes only by what crosses the line. Change in stock = inputs − outputs. This forest gains 9 kg of nitrogen per hectare each year. The line and the year must be stated before any adding.
scenes.visual: On screen: 'change in stock = inputs − outputs', then '14 − 5 = +9' under it. The counter ticks up +9 per year for three years (9, 18, 27).
scenes.narration: The store changes only by what crosses the line. Change in stock = inputs − outputs. This forest gains 9 kg of nitrogen per hectare each year. The line and the year must be stated before any adding.

scenes.tts: But most nitrogen never crosses the line at all. Decomposers release it from dead leaves as ammonium. Trees take it up, grow leaves, and drop them again.
scenes.visual: A GREY ring of arrows appears entirely inside the GOLD line: 'soil organic N' to 'ammonium' to 'trees' to 'falling leaves' and back to soil. TEAL blocks circulate round it.
scenes.narration: But most nitrogen never crosses the line at all. Decomposers release it from dead leaves as ammonium. Trees take it up, grow leaves, and drop them again.

scenes.tts: That loop moves about ninety kilograms per hectare each year. Here it is the biggest flux in the valley, far bigger than all the inputs together.
scenes.caption: That loop moves about 90 kg per hectare each year. Here it is the biggest flux in the valley, far bigger than all the inputs together.
scenes.visual: The GREY ring thickens and is labelled '90 kg N per hectare per year'. Beside it the two BLUE inputs bundle into one thin arrow labelled '14'. A bar pair: '90' bar about six times taller than the '14' bar (computed).
scenes.narration: That loop moves about 90 kg per hectare each year. Here it is the biggest flux in the valley, far bigger than all the inputs together.

scenes.tts: Yet the counter never sees it. Nitrogen leaving one pool in the loop enters another pool inside the same line. In the sum, those transfers cancel. Cancelling is bookkeeping. It does not mean the loop is small.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back so the whole GOLD line and the GREY ring inside it fill the frame. TEAL blocks go round the ring; none touches the line. The counter keeps ticking +9 per year, unmoved by the ring.
scenes.narration: Yet the counter never sees it. Nitrogen leaving one pool in the loop enters another pool inside the same line. In the sum, those transfers cancel. Cancelling is bookkeeping. It does not mean the loop is small.

scenes.tts: Now cut the trees, and keep new plants from growing. Does the loop simply stop, or does it go somewhere?
scenes.visual: The trees are felled and lie on the ground inside the line (label 'trees left on site'). The ring's 'uptake into trees' arrow flickers and goes dark. A question card: 'stop, or go somewhere?'
scenes.narration: Now cut the trees, and keep new plants from growing. Does the loop simply stop, or does it go somewhere?

scenes.visual: Hold on the broken ring; a timer circle fills over five seconds.

scenes.tts: It goes somewhere. Decomposers keep releasing nitrogen, but no roots take it up. Microbes turn the extra ammonium into nitrate, which soil holds weakly.
scenes.visual: The decomposer arrow keeps running at full width; TEAL blocks pile up in the 'ammonium' box, then relabel to 'nitrate' and slide loose from soil particles.
scenes.narration: It goes somewhere. Decomposers keep releasing nitrogen, but no roots take it up. Microbes turn the extra ammonium into nitrate, which soil holds weakly.

scenes.tts: So the loop breaks open and spills across the line. Nitrate pours out in the stream, and the counter turns negative.
scenes.visual: The GREY arrows bend downslope and exit through the GOLD line as one fat RED stream arrow labelled 'stream nitrate'. The counter swings from positive to negative values (schematic size).
scenes.narration: So the loop breaks open and spills across the line. Nitrate pours out in the stream, and the counter turns negative.

scenes.tts: Likens, Bormann and colleagues saw this at Hubbard Brook, in New Hampshire. The stream from their cut watershed carried far more nitrate and calcium than the uncut one.
scenes.visual: Map pin 'Hubbard Brook, New Hampshire'. Two valleys side by side: 'cut, regrowth suppressed' and 'uncut reference'. The cut valley's RED stream arrow is much fatter, labelled 'nitrate' and 'calcium'. Label 'schematic; direction, not size'.
scenes.narration: Likens, Bormann and colleagues saw this at Hubbard Brook, in New Hampshire. The stream from their cut watershed carried far more nitrate and calcium than the uncut one.

scenes.tts: Rain brought in no more nitrogen than before. The forest's own recycled nitrogen was leaving. A store changes only across its boundary, and here the broken loop crossed it.
scenes.visual: The cut valley alone: the BLUE rain input unchanged in width, the GREY ring now draining out as the RED stream arrow. On-screen line: 'rain input unchanged; the loop leaked out'.
scenes.narration: Rain brought in no more nitrogen than before. The forest's own recycled nitrogen was leaving. A store changes only across its boundary, and here the broken loop crossed it.

scenes.visual: Hex end card with one line: 'Stores change only across the boundary; a broken loop can cross it.'
